title: December, 2004
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: Does Chloe come home. An email. The strip draws an email for the first time and hates it.

panels.composition: The garage. The monitor. An email open. WOOD reading. BARNABY. Two stick figures pretending not to read it.

image.prompt: a young man reading an email on a bulky monitor in his garage, a small dog, two small stick figures at the back of the panel pretending not to look, muddy digital flats

panels.composition: The email, drawn as a panel: a plain text box. 'W — Chicago for Christmas. Work. It's not Europe. It's not there either. Tell the dog. — C.' No handwriting. The strip draws the font. It hates the font.

image.prompt: a panel that is a plain email window in a blocky early-2000s system font, short message, the whole thing drawn with visible distaste
image.notes: Letter after. The strip's first typed Chloe. The handwriting is gone.

balloons.text: She used to write so small you needed a lamp. Now it's Arial.

image.prompt: a young man turning from his monitor to tell a dog something, wounded about a font

panels.composition: Wood printing the email. Pinning the printout to the corkboard by one corner, like the cardstock one. It hangs there looking like nothing.

image.prompt: a young man pinning a printed email to a crowded corkboard by one corner so it hangs free beside old handwritten postcards, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor

notes: She does not come home. The first email. The strip mourns the handwriting.
